newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela plans tour of South East Asia.
newsitem.headline: Mandela plans tour of South East Asia.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela will lead a business delegation to Southeast Asia next month to promote investment and development aid to South Africa, the Department of Foreign Affairs said on Friday.

Mandela will visit Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei and the Philippines for a six-day tour starting on October 12. In all four countries, he will be hosted by heads of state and meet political and business leaders.
Southeast Asia has gained increasing importance for post-apartheid South Africa in terms of two-way trade and source of investment.
Trade with the four countries Mandela is to visit amounted to over four billion rand ($883 million) in 1995, the Foreign Affairs department said in a statement.
Malaysian businessmen have blazed an acquisition trail across South Africa in the past two years, pumping resources into sectors ranging from property to energy, food and banking.
Malaysians have become South Africa's fourth biggest direct investors, pumping in 1.8 billion rand between April 1994 -- when democratic elections were held -- and May 1996.

This does not include Malaysia's largest investment in South Africa so far, the 1.9 billion rand purchase in June by state-owned oil company Petronas Berhad of a 30 percent stake in South Africa's energy company, Engen Ltd .

Bilateral trade between Singapore and South Africa rose to 2.3 billion rand last year, sharply up from the 1.5 billion rand total in 1994. Of the 1995 overall, South Africa exported goods worth 1.12 billion rand to Singapore.
